standard.title: Analyse information and identify perspectives
standard.description: analyse information and data, and identify perspectives
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2S03-S04): Students compared objects and activities and discussed perspectives of different groups.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse information and data to identify evidence of change and identify perspectives in sources.

nodes.label: Comparing sources to identify change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare information across different sources to identify evidence of change and continuity.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare at least two sources on the same topic and identify at least one piece of evidence of change or continuity.
nodes.typical_width: Compare images and maps of the local area over time; compare accounts of historic events to determine effects of changes; use visible thinking strategies to examine paintings and maps across time periods.
wider: Compare three or more sources from different time periods on the same topic and describe the trajectory of change
Evaluate which sources are most reliable for understanding a specific change and explain why
nodes.hinge_reason: Comparative source analysis is the foundational move for all historical analysis — students who cannot compare sources for evidence cannot identify perspectives or draw sound conclusions.

response_modes.reason: Source comparison requires a structured approach — use visible thinking protocols (See-Think-Wonder, compare-contrast matrices) to scaffold before expecting independent analysis.

success_criteria: Compares at least two sources on the same topic
Identifies at least one piece of evidence of change or continuity

nodes.label: Identifying perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify different perspectives in sources and explain what shapes each perspective.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different perspectives on the same event or issue from provided sources.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse information from interviews with different people about rules and decisions; compare different accounts of historic events; identify whose perspective is represented in a source and what it might omit.
wider: Identify whose perspectives are absent from a set of sources and discuss why they might be missing
Analyse a set of paintings and maps to explore evidence of whose worldview is represented

response_modes.reason: Multiple perspectives on the same topic reveal the constructed nature of historical accounts — use interviews, photographs and written sources together for genuine breadth.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Identifying whose perspectives are absent from sources is as important as identifying whose are present — this is a key historical thinking skill that transforms source analysis.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two different perspectives on the same topic
Explains what might shape each perspective
